evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: The `manager_restarted` check only verifies that the manager PID and invocation ID are nonempty and changed. A guest reboot changes both values, so a reboot can satisfy this check even without a manager restart; a later reboot can still satisfy the separate `boot_id_changed` check. The snapshots already carry boot IDs (as used by `boot_id_changed`), so requiring nonempty equal boot IDs on the manager before/after snapshots is a minimal correctness fix to ensure the manager restart is bound to the same guest boot.
